## Wave 1 Summary

The framework measured the *parameter-space* geometry of its eigenbundles to death — Berry curvature ≡ 0 on the Jensen line (S25), Chern = 0 (S96 P-30w), Euler = 0 (S105 W3-1), 11+ independent topological invariants all trivial — while leaving the *spectral-correlation* geometry of the eigenvalues themselves under-measured at the discriminating level. The only prior spectral-statistics datum is CHAOS-1 (single-particle ⟨r⟩=0.321, pooled ⟨r⟩=0.422; both integrable-leaning) and an S46 spectral-form-factor INFO (γ-pattern, later batch-MIGRATED in S81). Neither resolved the Poisson / RMT / arithmetic-chaos question via the *discriminating* observables: the connected spectral form factor ramp, the number-variance Σ²(L) growth law, the small-s level-repulsion exponent, and the sector-resolved-vs-pooled spacing distribution. This wave attacks that asymmetry. It translates seed convergence #2 (spectral statistics ↔ integrability) into two compute gates (W1-1 SFF/number-variance; W1-2 P(s) sector-resolved), and seed berry steps 3-4 (catastrophe germ census; second-Chern Yang-monopole over the off-block C² coset) into two more — the two remaining un-measured geometric objects on the eigenbundle side. Gate-type mix: compute × 4.

## §W1-1. INV3-W1-1

```yaml
gate_id: "INV3-W1-1"
schema_version: "R3"
gate_type: "compute"
trigger: "[SIGN]"
classification: "GEOMETRIC"
agent_type: "kitaev-quantum-chaos-theorist"
hypothesis: "The connected spectral form factor K(τ) and the number variance Σ²(L) of the unfolded D_K spectrum at τ_fold discriminate Poisson (Σ²~L linear growth, NO RMT ramp in K(τ)) from RMT (Σ²~ln L logarithmic, linear ramp) from arithmetic chaos (super-logarithmic Σ², arithmetic/non-linear ramp) — the framework's integrability is supported-but-not-closed at the discriminating-observable level."

method:
  description: >
    Load the τ_fold=0.19 L12 spectrum cache (unique eigenvalues with multiplicity).
    (1) UNFOLD: build the cumulative counting function N(λ) and rescale to unit mean
    level density via a smooth Weyl fit (polynomial degree pinned below; the staircase
    minus its smooth part), so the unfolded spectrum {x_n} has mean spacing 1. Unfolding
    is done PER (p,q) Peter-Weyl block then concatenated (block-diagonality of D_K means
    cross-block spacings are an artifact of pooling — see W1-2; for K(τ)/Σ²(L) the
    canonical object is the UNFOLDED-then-pooled spectrum, with the per-block unfolding
    removing the trivial multi-component superposition trend). (2) CONNECTED SFF:
    K(τ) = ⟨|Σ_n e^{2πi x_n τ}|²⟩ − |Σ_n e^{2πi x_n τ}⟨⟩|² , i.e. the connected
    correlator with the smooth (disconnected) part subtracted; average over a τ-window
    and over spectral sub-windows for the ensemble ⟨⟩_c. (3) NUMBER VARIANCE:
    Σ²(L) = ⟨n(L)²⟩ − ⟨n(L)⟩² where n(L) counts unfolded levels in a randomly placed
    interval of length L; scan L over the pinned range. (4) SPECTRAL RIGIDITY:
    Δ₃(L) = ⟨ min_{A,B} (1/L) ∫ [N(x)−A−Bx]² dx ⟩ (Dyson–Mehta), the least-squares
    staircase rigidity. (5) DISCRIMINATE: fit Σ²(L) growth exponent p in Σ²(L) ∝ L^p
    over the linear-response window and read off the ramp presence in K(τ).
  producing_script: "computations/investigation-3/inv3_w1_sff_numvar.py"

operator:
  type: "inequality"
  form: >
    p_Sigma2 := d ln Σ²(L) / d ln L over the pinned window.
    PASS-Poisson iff p_Sigma2 ∈ [0.85, 1.15] (linear, Σ²~L) AND no RMT ramp
    (K(τ) shows no sustained linear-in-τ rise above the Poisson plateau K_Poisson(τ)→N·(2τ−... ) baseline);
    FAIL-RMT iff p_Sigma2 ≤ 0.5 (logarithmic, Σ²~ln L) AND a sustained linear ramp present;
    INFO-arithmetic iff 0.5 < p_Sigma2 < 0.85 (super-log but sub-linear) OR a non-linear/arithmetic ramp signature.

strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "p_Sigma2 ∈ [0.85, 1.15] (Poisson linear-growth band) with no RMT ramp"
  direction: "="

boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: "Poisson Σ²(L)=L exactly (uncorrelated levels, Mehta RMT ch.16); RMT GUE Σ²(L)=(1/π²)(ln(2πL)+γ_E+1) ~ ln L; the L^1 vs ln L separation is the analytic discriminator boundary"

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: "continuous — p_Sigma2 is a fitted real exponent; the PASS band [0.85,1.15] is a continuous interval"

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "78080"                         # unique eigenvalues in the L12 τ_fold cache (full set used)
  L_max: "12"                             # spectrum cache truncation (cross-check at L_max=14)
  scan_range: "[0.5, 20.0]"               # number-variance interval length L window (unfolded mean-spacing units)
  step_size: "0.25"                       # L-grid step for Σ²(L)/Δ₃(L); τ-grid for K(τ): 512 points on [0, 2] (Heisenberg-time-normalized)
  tolerance: "0.15"                       # half-width of the Poisson p_Sigma2=1.0 PASS band
  scheme: "connected-SFF-Dyson-Mehta-numvar"
  convention: "RATIO"                     # exponent p is a dimensionless log-log slope ratio
  random_seed: "20260614"                 # for the random interval placements in Σ²(L) ensemble average + spectral-window bootstrap
  GPU_path: "torch.linalg"               # K(τ) = |Σ e^{iEτ}|² via torch.matmul over (τ-grid × eigenvalue) phase matrix on cuda; per CLAUDE math-scripts ≥100×100
  unfold_poly_degree: "7"                # smooth Weyl-fit polynomial degree for the per-block staircase unfolding (pinned; not adaptive)
  unfold_mode: "per-(p,q)-block-then-pool" # block-diagonality of D_K: unfold each Peter-Weyl block separately, concatenate; removes trivial superposition trend
  n_spectral_windows: "16"               # number of disjoint spectral sub-windows for the ⟨⟩_c ensemble average
  publication_precision: "4"             # p_Sigma2 published to 4 sig figs; downstream INV3 cites it

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "Poisson statistics give Σ²(L) growing LINEARLY in L (slope p=1) and NO RMT
            ramp in K(τ); RMT gives Σ²(L) growing LOGARITHMICALLY (slope p→0 over a decade)
            and a LINEAR ramp; therefore the fitted slope p_Sigma2 and the ramp presence
            jointly classify the spectrum's universality class."
    Definition 1: Σ²(L) := ⟨n(L)²⟩ − ⟨n(L)⟩²,  n(L) = # unfolded levels in an interval of length L
                  [number variance; Mehta, Random Matrices, ch.16; unfolded ⇒ ⟨n(L)⟩ = L]
    Definition 2: K(τ) := ⟨ |Σ_n e^{2πi x_n τ}|² ⟩_c   [connected spectral form factor; the
                  Fourier transform of the connected two-level correlator R_2^c(x); {x_n} unfolded]
    Definition 3 (Poisson): uncorrelated levels ⇒ R_2^c(x) = δ(x) ⇒ Σ²_Poisson(L) = L
                  and K_Poisson(τ) = N (flat in τ, NO ramp — the disconnected part is subtracted)
                  [Berry–Tabor: a generic integrable system has Poisson statistics]
    Definition 4 (GUE/RMT): R_2^c(x) = −(sin πx / πx)² (level repulsion) ⇒
                  Σ²_GUE(L) = (1/π²)[ln(2πL) + γ_E + 1] ~ ln L (logarithmic);
                  K_GUE(τ) = N·min(τ,1)·2 − ... rises LINEARLY (the "ramp") up to the
                  Heisenberg time τ=1 then plateaus [Mehta ch.6]
    Substitute (form the discriminating quantity):
                  p_Sigma2 := d ln Σ²(L) / d ln L
    Simplify (Poisson):  Σ²=L ⇒ ln Σ² = ln L ⇒ p_Sigma2 = 1  EXACTLY
    Simplify (RMT):      Σ² = c·ln L ⇒ ln Σ² = ln c + ln(ln L) ⇒
                         p_Sigma2 = d ln(ln L)/d ln L = 1/ln L → 0 over a decade of L
    Canonical form:      p_Sigma2|_Poisson = 1  ;  p_Sigma2|_RMT → 0  ;  the two are
                         separated by the band boundary p_Sigma2 = 0.85 (PASS-Poisson)
                         vs p_Sigma2 ≤ 0.5 (FAIL-RMT)
    Direction:           LARGER p_Sigma2 ⇒ MORE Poisson-like (linear growth) ⇒ MORE integrable;
                         the RMT ramp in K(τ) is the COMPLEMENTARY signature (present ⇒ chaotic).
                         A super-log-but-sub-linear p_Sigma2 ∈ (0.5, 0.85) with an arithmetic
                         (non-linear) ramp is the arithmetic-chaos INFO signature (Berry, Bogomolny).
    Conclusion:          the fitted p_Sigma2 and the ramp presence jointly classify the spectrum;
                         the framework's expected integrability (Berry–Tabor; prior CHAOS-1 ⟨r⟩
                         integrable-leaning) predicts PASS-Poisson; the gate measures whether the
                         DISCRIMINATING observables confirm it or reveal arithmetic-chaos structure.
```

## §W1-2. INV3-W1-2

```yaml
gate_id: "INV3-W1-2"
schema_version: "R3"
gate_type: "compute"
trigger: "[SIGN]"
classification: "GEOMETRIC"
agent_type: "kitaev-quantum-chaos-theorist"
hypothesis: "The nearest-neighbor spacing distribution P(s) of the D_K spectrum at τ_fold, fitted to semi-Poisson and Berry–Robnik forms, distinguishes a POOLING ARTIFACT (the pooled spectrum is a superposition of independent block spectra ⇒ small-s exponent ≈0, P(s)→e^{−s} Poisson) from INTRINSIC intermediate statistics (a single Peter-Weyl (p,q) block shows genuine small-s level repulsion, P(s)~s^β with β≈1 semi-Poisson) — the ⟨r⟩=0.422 pooled value above Poisson 0.3863 is decided one way or the other by going SECTOR-RESOLVED."

method:
  description: >
    Load the τ_fold=0.19 L12 cache WITH its Peter-Weyl (p,q) block labels (each eigenvalue
    tagged by the irrep block it came from; D_K is block-diagonal so this labelling is exact).
    (1) POOLED P(s): unfold the full pooled spectrum, compute the nearest-neighbor spacing
    distribution, fit to (a) Poisson e^{−s}, (b) semi-Poisson P(s)=4s e^{−2s}, (c) Berry–Robnik
    P(s;ρ) (the ρ-mixed Poisson⊕GOE gap distribution), extracting the small-s repulsion
    exponent β (P(s)∝s^β as s→0) and the Berry–Robnik fraction ρ. (2) SECTOR-RESOLVED P(s):
    for each (p,q) block with ≥ N_min levels, unfold THAT block alone and compute its P(s)
    + small-s β; aggregate the per-block β distribution. (3) DISCRIMINATE: if the pooled
    spectrum is a trivial superposition of independent integrable blocks, the per-block β
    is ≈0 (each block Poisson) AND the pooled P(s)→Poisson (superposition of independents
    → Poisson, the Berry–Robnik ρ→1 limit). If the intermediate statistics are INTRINSIC,
    the per-block β≈1 (semi-Poisson within each block). The ⟨r⟩ statistic is computed per
    block and pooled as a cross-check against the canonical r_POISSON=0.3863 / r_GOE=0.5307.
  producing_script: "computations/investigation-3/inv3_w1_ps_sector.py"

operator:
  type: "inequality"
  form: >
    β_block := mean small-s repulsion exponent of the per-(p,q)-block P(s) (P(s)∝s^β as s→0).
    PASS-pooling-artifact iff β_block ∈ [−0.15, 0.30] (each block ≈Poisson, intermediate stats are a pooling artifact)
      AND pooled Berry–Robnik ρ ≥ 0.85 (pooled spectrum near-Poisson);
    INFO-intrinsic-semi-Poisson iff β_block ∈ [0.70, 1.30] (genuine within-block linear repulsion);
    FAIL-intrinsic-GOE iff β_block ≥ 1.70 (within-block quadratic/cubic repulsion, RMT-class).

strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "β_block ∈ [−0.15, 0.30] (per-block Poisson; intermediate pooled stats = superposition artifact) with pooled ρ ≥ 0.85"
  direction: "="

boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: "Poisson P(s)=e^{−s} ⇒ β=0 exactly; semi-Poisson P(s)=4s·e^{−2s} ⇒ β=1; GOE P(s)=(π/2)s·e^{−πs²/4} ⇒ β=1; GUE β=2; superposition-of-independents theorem: pooling M independent spectra → Poisson as M→∞ (Mehta ch.16) — this IS the pooling-artifact null"

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: true
  mesh_density: "β reference values are integers/half-integers {0 (Poisson), 1 (semi-Poisson, GOE), 2 (GUE)}; the fitted β is continuous, the discriminating reference mesh is integer"

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "78080"                         # unique eigenvalues in the pooled spectrum
  L_max: "12"
  scan_range: "N/A — set membership over (p,q) blocks, not a parameter scan"
  step_size: "N/A — per-block enumeration"
  tolerance: "0.30"                       # upper edge of the per-block-Poisson β band (PASS if β ≤ 0.30)
  scheme: "P-of-s-semiPoisson-BerryRobnik-fit-sector-resolved"
  convention: "RATIO"                     # β is a dimensionless small-s log-slope exponent
  random_seed: "20260614"                 # bootstrap resampling of P(s) histograms for β-fit error bars
  GPU_path: "cpu-cap-OMP8"               # per-block spacing histograms + small-block curve fits are small; CPU with OMP cap (no ≥100×100 dense linear algebra)
  unfold_poly_degree: "7"                # smooth Weyl-fit degree for staircase unfolding (matches W1-1)
  N_min_block: "50"                       # minimum levels for a (p,q) block to be sector-resolved (small-N blocks pooled into a diagnostic-only residual class)
  small_s_fit_window: "[0.0, 0.5]"       # s-window for the P(s)∝s^β small-s exponent fit (unfolded mean-spacing units)
  berry_robnik_init_rho: "0.5"           # initial guess for the Berry–Robnik ρ fit (not the result; deterministic LM start)
  publication_precision: "3"             # β_block + ρ published to 3 sig figs

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "A pooled spectrum that is a SUPERPOSITION of independent integrable block-spectra
            has Poisson statistics (small-s exponent β=0) EVEN IF each block individually had
            repulsion; therefore the small-s exponent of a SINGLE block (β_block), not the
            pooled exponent, decides whether the intermediate statistics are intrinsic."
    Definition 1: P(s) := nearest-neighbor spacing distribution of the unfolded spectrum
                  [s = (x_{n+1} − x_n), mean ⟨s⟩=1 after unfolding]
    Definition 2: β := small-s repulsion exponent, P(s) ∝ s^β as s → 0
                  [β=0 Poisson (no repulsion); β=1 semi-Poisson & GOE; β=2 GUE]
    Definition 3 (superposition theorem): if a spectrum is the union of M statistically
                  INDEPENDENT sub-spectra, then as M grows the pooled P(s) → e^{−s} (Poisson),
                  REGARDLESS of each sub-spectrum's own statistics [Mehta ch.16; the
                  level-sequence superposition law]
    Definition 4 (block-diagonality): D_K = ⊕_{(p,q)} D_{(p,q)} (Peter-Weyl), so the pooled
                  spectrum IS a superposition of the independent block spectra [framework
                  structural theorem, S22b/S33]
    Substitute: pooled small-s exponent β_pooled is driven toward 0 by Definition 3+4
                EVEN IF β_block > 0 inside each block.
    Simplify:   the DISCRIMINATING quantity is β_block (single-block exponent), not β_pooled:
                  β_block ≈ 0  ⇒ each block intrinsically Poisson ⇒ intermediate pooled stats
                               (⟨r⟩=0.422 > 0.3863) are a POOLING ARTIFACT (superposition)
                  β_block ≈ 1  ⇒ each block has genuine linear repulsion ⇒ semi-Poisson is
                               INTRINSIC (the substrate's within-sector statistics are
                               intermediate, not Poisson)
    Canonical form: PASS-pooling-artifact ⇔ β_block ≤ 0.30 ∧ ρ ≥ 0.85;
                    INFO-intrinsic-semi-Poisson ⇔ β_block ∈ [0.70, 1.30]
    Direction:  LARGER β_block ⇒ MORE intrinsic within-sector repulsion ⇒ LESS purely
                integrable at the single-sector level. The pooled ⟨r⟩=0.422 sitting ABOVE
                Poisson 0.3863 is EXPLAINED as a superposition/unfolding residual (Track A)
                OR as genuine intermediate statistics (Track B) precisely by the sign of
                (β_block − 0.30).
    Conclusion: going SECTOR-RESOLVED converts the ambiguous pooled ⟨r⟩ datum into a decisive
                test; the per-block β_block is the observable that the prior pooled-only
                CHAOS-1 computation could not isolate.

input_files:
  canonical_constants:
    path: "computations/_shared/canonical_constants.py"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"
  spectrum_cache_L12:
    path: "computations/session-84/s84_spectrum_cache_L12_tau019.npz"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"
  spectrum_cache_L14:
    path: "computations/session-87/s87_spectrum_cache_L14_tau019.npz"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"

fb_pair:
```

## Wave 1 → Wave 2 Decision Point

Wave 2 (heat-kernel scale-transport & spectral rigidity, owner spectral-geometer) is independent of Wave 1 outputs — the two waves attack orthogonal axes (eigenvalue-correlation + eigenbundle-topology geometry vs heat-trace dimensionful-axis machinery) and dispatch in parallel. No Wave-1 verdict gates any Wave-2 gate. The only soft coupling is thematic: if INV3-W1-1/W1-2 return PASS-Poisson / PASS-pooling-artifact (confirming Berry–Tabor integrability at the discriminating level), that strengthens the spectral-geometer's UB-5 "integrability as an under-exploited strength" reading, which Wave 2's INV3-W2-4 (Weyl-law oscillatory remainder → non-variational route to τ_fold) builds on. This coupling is informational, not a dispatch prerequisite; both waves run concurrently.

Per-outcome routing for downstream investigation synthesis (`/rclab-investigate --investigation 3`):
- **INV3-W1-1 / W1-2**: PASS (Poisson / pooling-artifact) → consolidate into a Berry–Tabor integrability finding for session-promotion. INFO (arithmetic / intrinsic-semi-Poisson) → flag a NEW intermediate-statistics characterization (Berry–Robnik) as a workshop seed. FAIL (RMT) → a major constraint-map inversion, escalate to a dedicated adjudication.
- **INV3-W1-3**: PASS-A2 → fold-germ confirmed, report the diabolical-point census (G-B2). INFO-A3 → a new cusp/Pearcey catastrophe-optics result, session-promotion candidate.
- **INV3-W1-4**: PASS c₂=0 → triviality extends to the broken base (strengthens the metric-without-curvature wall; feeds HY1 atlas-05 W5 qualification). PASS c₂≠0 → Yang monopole, the first non-trivial eigenbundle invariant, high-leverage session-promotion. FAIL/INFO → re-derivation carry-forward.
